title: Censorinus calendar authority and correction-state constructor
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED, NOT SELECTED. Censorinus De die natali XX describes successive calendar states: ten months/304 days, a twelve-month 355-day year against a 354-day lunar year, a 22/23-day intercalary month every two years, pontifical discretionary distortion for magistrate and tax interests, Caesar's 445-day correction, and the later 365-day solar rule with a leap day every four years. A finite writer carries one calendar state and its correction authority. It predicts a different later date/term outcome from a neutral fixed month-length or permanently biennial-intercalation rival.

source.source_span: Lines 227–249 of the linked translation cover the Roman calendar history, and lines 241–247 cover biennial intercalation, pontifical discretion, Caesar's 445-day corrective year, and the fixed solar/leap-day rule.
source.provenance: The linked LacusCurtius page is a public translation of Censorinus. The card uses its bounded source account and does not claim that its later editorial translation is a medieval target witness.

duplicate_screen.checked: FAMILY NUMBER_CALENDAR_AND_COUNTING; GDT354/GDT356 calendar history; prior month-length/ordinal templates.
duplicate_screen.difference: Those predecessors concern month-length, ordinal, or calendar-coordinate matching. This proposal makes authority, discretionary bias, and reform state the semantic payload; it is retained only as a distinct policy-state candidate and must be rejected if review shows that its only consequence is another number template.

component_functions.INIT: opens the civil/natural mismatch; it does not claim that civil and lunar lengths are identical.
component_functions.INTERCALATE: changes civil state by a declared 22/23-day insertion every two years in the old regime.
component_functions.BIAS: records that pontifical discretion can lengthen or shorten an office or tax-farm interval; it is not a free numerical correction.
component_functions.REFORM: closes the discretionary regime and opens Caesar's solar 365-day rule with a four-year leap-day branch.
component_functions.WHOLE_RESIDUAL: selects historical state transition (INIT, INTERCALATE, BIAS, REFORM) rather than assigning each numeral an isolated English value.

worked_example: effect_old = PROJECT(s3, magistrate_or_tax_due); effect_new = PROJECT(s4, same_due_type); retain 445_day correction as a historical transition, not a normal recurring year.
constructor.observable_consequence: A source-complete state reading predicts that the same office/tax reference can have a discretionary duration before reform, while after reform it follows the fixed solar/leap rule. A permanently neutral biennial calendar cannot produce the bias branch or the 445-day correction state.
rivals: MONTH_TEMPLATE: treats all calendar passages as fixed month lengths or ordinal values and loses authority/bias/reform scope.
PERMANENT_BIENNIAL: continues 22/23-day insertion after Caesar and therefore predicts the wrong later civil state.
constructor.falsifier: Reject if the candidate requires an independently assigned numeral meaning for every date, if the bias branch cannot alter a projected office/tax interval, or if it treats Caesar's 445-day correction as the ordinary post-reform year. The source does not identify a target calendar or target numbers.
constructor.target_binding_limit: No target calendar terms or numerical glyph values are claimed. The card is a raw source-grounded policy/state hypothesis and overlaps an existing calendar family by design; its only justification for retention is the authority and reform consequence.
